claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'Paragraph-name, IV-6, IV-7, IV-35' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Qualified, IV-19'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'Paragraph-name, IV-6, IV-7, IV-35' then '  Qualified, IV-19'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: page-971.md holds every index entry on its own line with sub-entries indented two spaces and continuations four (e.g. 'Paragraph-name, IV-6, IV-7, IV-35' then '  Qualified, IV-19', '  Reference format, IV-43'), exactly mirroring the printed one-entry-per-line, indented-sub-entry layout. The claim itself concedes the entry text and page references match the PDF. The only difference is how a Markdown renderer would reflow bare lines, and the inconsistency with the '- ' list style of pages 961-962: a formatting/rendering concern in an informative index, not a content discrepancy between PDF and transcription. No text is missing, misquoted, or changed in meaning.
